title: AWS CloudTrail (flAWS.cloud, WEAK labels)
label_description: WEAK, rule-based labels (not ground truth). An (identity, 1-hour) block is Anomaly if R1: >= 10 events with an AccessDenied/Unauthorized errorCode, or R2: a sensitive IAM write (Create*/Delete*/Attach*/Detach*/Put*/Update*/Add*/Remove*/Upload*/Set*/Change*) or S3 permission/policy change from a source IP first seen in the trace during that same hour.
warnings: Labels are WEAK and rule-based, NOT ground truth (see label_description). Precision/recall measure agreement with the rule, not with real attacks.

The rule keys on authorization errors and new IPs; the model's features (dominant event/component/IP codes, event count, hour) only partly overlap with it, so disagreement can mean the rule is wrong as often as the model.

The shared HDFSDataCleaner removed 713,423 exact-duplicate rows (36.8% of recognized records): records repeating the same eventID, time, caller, action, source IP and errorCode, i.e. duplicate deliveries of one event, so removing them is correct de-duplication.
block_definition: (identity, 1-hour window): the caller's ARN/key/principal, or anonymous@<ip>, per clock hour.
evaluation_protocol: stratified 70/30 train/test; all metrics on test

labels.rule: WEAK, rule-based labels (not ground truth). An (identity, 1-hour) block is Anomaly if R1: >= 10 events with an AccessDenied/Unauthorized errorCode, or R2: a sensitive IAM write (Create*/Delete*/Attach*/Detach*/Put*/Update*/Add*/Remove*/Upload*/Set*/Change*) or S3 permission/policy change from a source IP first seen in the trace during that same hour.

trade_off.criterion: Pareto front on (test precision, mean lead over true alerts); best = highest expected_lead_per_alert (precision x mean true-alert lead) on the front
